subject: Realtime delivery slowdown — guidance and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Zhou <ethan.zhou@veloxai.com>, support@veloxai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime delivery slowdown — guidance and next steps

Hi Ethan / VeloxAI ops team,

We saw an increase in end-to-end latency for realtime delivery (streaming token SSE/WS responses) starting ~08:50 PDT that affected ~12% of requests routed to the us-west shard. You may have seen partial or delayed token delivery in interactive flows. We’ve opened an incident (RED-2027-045) and wanted to share immediate customer-facing mitigations so your engineers can reduce user impact while we stabilize.

Quick mitigations you can apply immediately:
- Switch to non-streaming polling (Responses API with wait_for_completion=true) for critical paths — this avoids partial-tokens being delayed by the streaming pipeline.
- Lower max_tokens (suggested delta: -25%) and reduce top_p / temperature to reduce decode time spikes.
- Prefer rwd-medium-8k (quantized) or rwd-small-4k variants for short-turn workloads to reduce inference latency.
- If you use client-side tail timeout, increase it from 4s -> 8s while we investigate.

What we’re doing: routing adjustments to drain affected us-west nodes, kernel patch rollout to reduce kv-cache contention, and targeted autoscaling triggers. ETA for initial remediation: ~2–3 hours. We’ll provide a timeline CSV and a PDF playbook in the next message.

If you want a private channel now, say the word and we’ll set up a direct Slack room with SRE and your ops.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0182

Ethan — answers inline and additional notes.

1) Impact: ~12% of streaming responses experienced delayed token delivery (tokens arriving in multi-second lumps). Full request timeouts were rare (~0.4%). So majority is stutter/partial delivery rather than hard fails.

2) Polling recommendation: switch to wait_for_completion=true on the Responses API for mission-critical flows. Redwood will still decode on the same backend but will hold partial frames until completion, which avoids user-visible stutter. Please increase client-side request timeout to 12s for the affected flows while we stabilize.

Additional tactical options:
- If you use chunked streaming with client-side reassembly, add idempotency checks for partial updates; send progress indicators to users.
- Temporarily route chat sessions to our dedicated pool if you have an account-level routing policy; we can move a subset of traffic and report latency delta.

I attached the incident timeline CSV and a short mitigation playbook (realtime-mitigation-playbook.pdf) with exact API snippets, sample curl payloads, and suggested guardrails.

ETA update: SREs expect kernel patch in canary by 11:30 PDT; broad rollout by 14:30 PDT assuming no regressions.

Diego

Attachment: realtime-mitigation-playbook.pdf

Ethan — Monica from Customer Success here. I’m escalating to our credits/finance team for a targeted service credit given the degradation window.

Operational next steps we propose:
- Create private Slack: redwood-veloxai-incident (SRE, Diego, Marissa, Monica + your ops). Please confirm the list of VeloxAI emails you want invited.
- Schedule a 30m post-incident review (we recommend 48–72h after stable) — we’ll include a preliminary impact estimate (attached xlsx) and remediation notes.
- We can enable temporary explicit routing to a dedicated pool (requires your consent for traffic split). If you grant it, we’ll move up to 20% of sessions to the dedicated pool immediately and monitor latency.

Let us know what you want to do and we’ll take care of the ops work ASAP.

— Monica
